normal.name: Why Not Zoidberg? 🦑
normal.text: I know I am the odd one out since Idol Culture has never been psychologically captivating for me. I see people actually posting how they are GRIEVING for Bioware and for me that is just a... what? Some of them are even starting to sound like soccer fanatics and that's an extra level of weird. I care about titles, not studios. I care about songs, not artists. And so on. Bioware's last game I liked was ME3. That's a LONG time ago. #Gaming #Bioware

normal.text: The Vega card memory allocation in work here. It's not magical, but if you hit the memory ceiling you don't have a devastating performance drop you have on more modern cards. On Windows you have need to enable the function manually, with a performace hit (because windows is crap), but on Linux is dynamically allocated on demand without user intervention, I read. But if you are still playing on Windows, you are shooting on your feet anyway. :trollface: https://invidious.tiekoetter.com/watch?v=mlUS7xfqeKc #pcgaming

normal.name: Marcus Adams
normal.text: #Valve also seems to have updated their built-in video editor for #Steam gameplay footage to include support for in-game events. #Deadlock, for example, shows loading screens with a striped texture on the timeline, and also places markers on the timeline for all kinds of events such as kills, towers being destroyed, etc. It had markers for screenshots and achievements before, but now games themselves can mark in-game events on the timeline, so that's awesome. #Gaming #PCGaming
normal.media: image: A screenshot of the Steam video clip editor, showing various markers along the timeline.
